newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa awards Saldanha port upgrade contracts.
newsitem.headline: South Africa awards Saldanha port upgrade contracts.

text.p: South African state port authority Portnet has awarded two contracts worth 82 million rand to upgrade Saldanha Bay to handle imports and exports from Iscor Ltd's Saldanha Steel Project.

A joint venture between Murray & Roberts Construction and LAMA International Contractors has been awarded a 36 million rand contract to build a 320 meter extension to the general cargo quay in the harbour.
Boskalis SA has been awarded a 45.8 million rand contract to dredge the approach channel and turning basin for the new quay.
Construction on the 6.8 billion Saldanha Steel Project started earlier this year and the first steel is expected in the first half of 1998 and the first iron in the second half of that year.

After a signing ceremony for the M&R-LAMA contract, Saki Macozoma, managing director of transport parastatal Transnet told Reuters that the upgrade was part of a new drive to build capacity in South Africa's ports.
"Over the years with sanctions, we were not trading legitimately with the world and we put very little resources into developing our ports," Macozoma said.
LAMA chief executive Harry Nieman said that the Saldanha project would help South Africa rebuild its marine construction skills which had been neglected over the last 10 years.

"Due to the lack of activity here, we have had something like 95 percent of our turnover in the last 10 years coming from our overseas activities mainly in the Far East, Hong Kong Malaysia and Thailand," Nieman said,

Macozoma said discussions were underway on upgrades at several other ports such as Durban and Richards Bay as well as the development of a new deep-water port in the Eastern Cape to service the planned Coega industrial development zone.
A feasibility study would be undertaken into the Coega project and a decision was expected by April next year.
The only other major port development in South Africa in recent years has been a 120 million rand contract awarded this year to extend a new quay in Richards Bay.
